## 2026-11-16 17:35 - The bench lost its only write path: the vendor loader cannot boot our slot A and cannot be prompted

The reset hold did not buy a recovery, it exposed the floor. The capture
`build/uart-logs/20261116T103014Z-recover-3dk.log` holds the cycle: U-Boot tries A
(`bootflag a bootreg 11`), the FIP fallback prints the image header and dies with a `data abort`
inside U-Boot (`r5=0x834d3bae`), it falls to B (`bootflag b bootreg 10`), the stock 4.1 MB kernel
starts, reaches `Run /init`, and panics at 10.8 s on the ShuangTa PCIe quirk in `jffs2_gcd_mtd15`.
The watchdog resets it into the next pass. The fault is not size: 3dg's 2.78 MB kernel reached the
same four header lines and aborted the same way, and 3dh's 2.96 MB kernel booted whenever it was
reached by the countdown path, which prints `alias console=...` and `Uncompressing Linux...`.
The countdown path is only reached when `bootreg` is 0 (POR sets `bootreg init, set 10`; the 05:23
recovery capture shows `bootreg 0` on that boot); the fallback path is entered whenever a slot is
flagged failed, and it corrupts the flags on its way through.

Two options were checked and closed. The serial prompt is unreachable: the 2026-11-08 floods with
and without `bootstopkey` both booted Linux, and `HARDWARE-IDENTITY.md` records that the router-side
RX pad never receives. A manual slot-A load from a network boot is also closed: `bootfip` is
`bootcmd` and the vendor env writes both slots with one image
(`fipupdate_eth=...mtd erase kernela;mtd write kernela...;mtd erase kernelb;mtd write kernelb...`
in `dumps/router-20261108/enva.bin`), so this loader accepts only a FIP package even when it is
handed one.

So the bench step is the vendor recovery: RESET held through power-on, `recovery.bin` over TFTP from
192.168.1.88, which is Cudy's own WR3000 v2 procedure
(https://www.cudy.com/en-gb/blogs/faq/how-to-recovery-the-cudy-router-from-openwrt-firmware-to-cudy-official-firmware).
The host lane passes a self-test: the server on UDP 69 answered a local RRQ for `recovery.bin`
(`421114c8ea999c925b7aa79cc548af81`, 20,975,775 bytes), `enp195s0f3u1` carries `192.168.1.88/24`,
and ufw allows `69/udp on enp195s0f3u1`. The stock-slot filesystem is also degraded (JFFS2 refuses
to erase blocks, the read-only squashfs returns ECC errors), so the recovery is wanted for its own
sake, not only as an unlock.

Left armed: the console capture (`timeout 600`) and the TFTP server; their PIDs and logs are in
`/tmp/arm-3dk.env` and `/tmp/arm-3dk-tftp.env`.

The durable rule for the next session: a slice can only be written while a booting userspace
exists, and a slice that does not boot costs a Cudy recovery, so every fire needs a recovery plan
before it is started. Procedure: `build/linux-kbuild/waves/3dk/recovery-3dk.md`.

## 2026-11-16 19:05 - Vendor stock restored; the recovery trigger was the RESET counter, and NetworkManager was stripping the host address

The box is back on the vendor image: OpenWrt 22.03.6 revision 2.4.15, stock kernel
`5.10.201 #0 SMP Sat Nov 25 18:18:57 2023`, 40 `hi_` modules, 2 wiphys
(`/sys/class/ieee80211/phy0`, `phy1`), the wireless calibration loaded on both bands
(`hwifi_rf_cali_file_load_2g succ`, `..._5g succ`, and the cali result written to the device on
both), `192.168.10.1` answering 2/2 pings, and SSH working on the project key.

The flash itself: `hi_upgrade 0x832808a4 0x1380279`, `upgrade soft version: 22.03.06`,
`Flashing kernel...` with the kernel slot erase at `0x0083ffff`, `Flashing rootfs...` writing
15,728,640 bytes with erases at `0x0173ffff` and `0x015fffff` - both kernel slots and both rootfs
partitions. Console: `build/uart-logs/20261116T115756Z-recover-stock.log`.

Two host-side faults cost attempts and are worth recording:

1. **The recovery trigger is the RESET button counter, not a plain hold.** The loader prints
   `RESET button is pressed for: 0 second(s)`, `1 second(s)`, `2 second(s)`, `Resetting...`, and only
   then does the countdown end in `recovery button press` followed by `Using pie@0x10a70000 device`,
   `TFTP from server 192.168.1.88; our IP address is 192.168.1.1`, `Filename 'recovery.bin'.`,
   `Load address: 0x83200000`. The counter only appears on a true power-on reset, never on the
   watchdog resets the box does itself. Evidence:
   `build/uart-logs/20261116T052326Z-recovery-boot.log` and `...2055749Z-plt-recovery.log`.
2. **NetworkManager strips the bench port's IPv4 addresses.** `enp195s0f3u1` sits in
   `connecting (getting IP configuration)`, retries DHCP against a board that is not serving it, and
   removes any address added by hand minutes later. With no address, the board's ARP for
   `192.168.1.88` is unanswered and the console shows `ARP Retry count exceeded; starting again`.
   The fix that held: `nmcli device set enp195s0f3u1 managed no`, then `ip addr add`. The port is
   still unmanaged now.

Correction to the earlier reading: I twice called an `RRQ` in the server log the board's request when
it was my own loopback self-test (`RRQ give up at block 1` is that test reading one block and
leaving). Only `RRQ ...` followed by `RRQ sent 20975775 bytes` from the board proves a transfer.

SSH after the flash needs the project key installed again (the recovered overlay is empty) and
dropbear started with `-R` after deleting the zero-byte host keys.

## 2026-11-17 08:45 - ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED: the 3dh kernel died in luofu_early's ioremap; 3dn boots to userspace, then wedges in a new userspace-stage problem

Diagnostic fire 3dm (3dl kernel + explicit earlycon in the built-in cmdline) gave the first readable
early boot. U-Boot read our uImage (Data Size 2964952), earlycon came up at 0x1010f000, and the
kernel panicked at 0.0 s:

    Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 00000010
    PC is at kmem_cache_alloc_trace+0xb4/0xd8     r5 = 0x00000000
    ioremap <- luofu_early+0x34 <- setup_arch <- start_kernel

Root cause: luofu_early() (the mach .init_early hook, called from setup_arch before mm_init) called
ioremap(). With the 3dh-era .config (CONFIG_SLAB=y + CONFIG_TRACING=y) kmalloc() compiles to
kmem_cache_alloc_trace(kmalloc_caches[..]) and the kmalloc caches do not exist yet, so the cache
pointer is NULL and the vm-area allocation NULL-derefs. The 3df/3dg builds had no CONFIG_TRACING,
which is why they booted; this is the exact 3dh regression, not a slot/delivery problem.

The panic rebooted (panic=5) into the stock fallback, which now booted healthy and stayed up.
Recovery detour: the guarded S99 hook from the first fire was renamed S99omo-recover.disabled but
procd matches S[0-9][0-9]*, so it kept restoring kernelb and rebooting (~6 cycles, each doing an mtd
write of the stock image). Moved it out of rc.d via the broker lane; kernelb md5 verified back to
stock 0ca1fde627aae581ef4e86441e968363; SSH restored by starting dropbear through the broker.

Fix: move the sysctrl crumb + bootreg flip out of luofu_early() into luofu_early_crumb()
(early_initcall, after mm_init, still before userspace). luofu_early() now only calls
luofu_uart_early(). Patched both the live tree and tools/lab-src (check-lab-src PASS) and built
3dn = 3dl config + earlycon + fix: luofu-slice-phase3dn.bin 3,005,332 B md5
984b0ac9f14a862e658b947665ff9a32, zImage 0e786a1da703d4c225a4e4aaec9ef26e, init 6464a08d (3dk
console-logging), DTB 336ba39e, trailer verified.

U-Boot Data Size 2964536, earlycon, luofu-fmc probe (FMC read path green in the same boot), 18
luofu partitions, Run /init at 14.45 s, the seven /vendor/upper ... OK lines, and procd at 19.54 s.
This is the first boot of the 3dh-era kernel class and it validates the fix.

New problem, same boot: after procd init (~19.5 s) there are no further userspace messages, and at
108 s/171 s the kernel reports rcu_sched stalls ("rcu_sched kthread starved ... cpu=0", 8407/14712

## 2026-11-17 20:40 - RE verdict: hyfi_bridging crash is a vendor sk_buff ABI mismatch, not the bridge hooks; v17 drops hyfi preload and fixes the hook variable ABI

Subagent RE (disassembly of hyfi-bridging.ko/khslink etc.):
- hyfi_netlink_receive (input callback of a vendor-private netlink protocol, id 30/26) does
  skb_clone(); r6 = [clone+0x118]; then stores into [r6+0x40]. That offset is vendor
  skb->data (0x118); in our kernel struct sk_buff is 0xb0 with data at 0xa0. So it reads out of
  bounds and faults. Measured vendor delta: len 0xc8 vs 0x54, data_len 0xcc vs 0x58, headers
  0x106/0x108/0x10a vs 0x8e/0x90/0x92, tail/end/head 0x10c/0x110/0x114 vs 0x94/0x98/0x9c,
  data 0x118 vs 0xa0 = +0x74 for len/data_len and +0x78 from headers on (4-byte vendor field
  between data_len and the bitfields). Anchors: hi_hslink_tx_urarp (skb_reserve), hyfi_bridge_get_dst
  (EtherType from head+mac_header), mc_find_acl_rule (len-data_len).
- The four br_* symbols are exported *pointer variables* in the vendor bridge, not functions:
  hyfi only stores callbacks into them (bridge_get_dst / port_dev_get / br_notify / mc_process).
  Our previous function stubs were ABI-wrong (a store would overwrite the stub's first
  instruction). Also the vendor bridge patches that would consume those pointers are not in our
  tree, so "real" hook semantics cannot be reconstructed offline.
- net_device side now matches (WEXT layout: priv_flags 0x13c, netdev_ops 0x128, sizeof 0x540);
  the remaining hyfi needs (net_bridge cache at netdev_priv+0x10, vendor skb private bytes) come
  from vendor-only bridge patches, i.e. a full vendor-bridge port, not a quick fix.

v17 (this build): remove hyfi-bridging from the preload list (it must not run on the vendor sk_buff
ABI), and replace the four exported function stubs with writable zeroed exported pointer variables.
No sk_buff ABI change. Slice 2,906,100 B md5 8342ccb9c0167766529277719330f43c (zImage a08ffc66,
init 74033a38). This is the "known-good stack without hyfi" test; the vendor userspace tolerated
hyfi's absence in the 2026-11-14 stack.

## 2026-11-18 09:15 - TEXT_OFFSET early-boot fix (patch 003): full 6.18 kernel compile RC=0 with the real, non-encodable offset; load address verified 0x80608000

Problem: textofs-$(CONFIG_ARCH_LUOFU) := 0x00608000 is required by the stock-loader address
derivation (stage 0x83200000 -> (stage & 0xf8000000) + TEXT_OFFSET = 0x80608000) but 0x00608000 is
not an encodable ARM rotated immediate, so stock 6.18 fails in arch/arm/kernel/head.S:123/:188
(pgtbl macro) and arch/arm/boot/compressed/head.S:312/:410 with "invalid constant (608000)".

Fix (opensource/target-skeleton/target/linux/hisilicon/patches-6.18/003-arm-textofs-nonimmediate.patch,
sha256 407352b8aced76da6c6f1fcef53c77bca0221473515c144126cbe3358e707f5c): use the kernel's own
mov_l macro to materialize TEXT_OFFSET instead of an immediate add/sub at the four sites:
- arch/arm/kernel/head.S: pgtbl macro -> mov_l rd, TEXT_OFFSET; add rd, rd, @phys; and the
  PHYS_OFFSET recovery -> mov_l r5, TEXT_OFFSET; sub r8, r8, r5.
- arch/arm/boot/compressed/head.S: final kernel image address -> mov_l r4, TEXT_OFFSET; add
  r4, r0, r4; and the zreladdr-relative adjustment -> mov_l r0, TEXT_OFFSET; sub r0, r4, r0.
mov_l expands to movw/movt on the target (CONFIG_CPU_V7) and to an ldr literal-pool load for older
CPUs; pristine-6.18.60 dry-run passes; no make override or WERROR workaround is used.

Verified in /home/shibbityshwab/openwrt-lab (openwrt main 27663a0, linux-6.18.60, tree's
OpenWrt GCC 14.4.0 toolchain): make target/linux/prepare RC=0 (patches 001/002/003 apply, no
.rej), make target/linux/compile -j16 RC=0; invalid-constant errors 0; arch/arm/boot/zImage
produced (sha256 45ad00d502ed7b2386f83db794e9015267f4f9d66de8d0deaab8aca24cf18d10).
Address story verified from the built artifacts: head objects compiled with
-DTEXT_OFFSET=0x00608000 (no override); vmlinux _text = 0xc0608000 with PAGE_OFFSET=0xc0000000;
linked stext recovers PHYS_OFFSET via adr_l _text + movw/movt 0x608000 (disasm
05-disasm-kernel-head.txt); physical _text = 0x80608000 == computed load address; uImage
mkdir must use -a/-e 0x80608000. An incremental rebuild (03b-rebuild) also RC=0.
Local-only evidence: build/linux-kbuild/waves/upstream-6.18-textoffset-20261118/ (00-README index,
baseline/fix logs and rc files, zImage sha, link/load derivation, kernel-head and compressed-head
disassemblies, pre-ARMv7 literal-pool fallback check, patch sha/dry-run). Gitignored; not
published; the zImage is an intermediate compile product, not a deliverable image.

  with [N] provenance markers; canonical re-derivation symbol-identical (286 symbols,
  KCONFIG_UNCHANGED). DTS rewritten to the bindings: CRG node is
  "hisilicon,luofu-crg","syscon","simple-mfd" with #clock-cells=1/#reset-cells=2 and only the
  watchdog child; no gate children, no vendor props, no duplicate unit address.

Design decisions:
- Shared 0x14880000 page: one syscon+simple-mfd node, one regmap; CRG driver and watchdog child
  both call syscon_node_to_regmap(), so neither maps or request_mem_region()s the page (0 call
  sites verified). This removes the lab bug where CRG claimed the page and the watchdog probe
  returned -EBUSY. Rejected: two nodes with overlapping reg + bare ioremap.
- Clock gates are a driver-side table indexed by dt-binding IDs (0..15 kept as ABI), not 16 fake
  child nodes without reg. Includes a missing-entry probe check.
- Reset cells kept 2-cell (CRG offset, bit), range-checked to 0x2c/0x30/0x34 so a specifier
  cannot write watchdog/softrst/mux/PLL words; rcdev.of_reset_n_cells=2 fixes the lab
  devm_reset_control_array_get() -EINVAL root cause.
- Watchdog: vendor value pairs/order preserved exactly (enable val1->val0 @0x64, stop val0->val1,
  ping reset0->reset1 @0x70, hwver-2 (secs-1) bits[18:10] @0x50 mask 0xfff803ff); probe performs
  zero register accesses; no restart handler (vendor sysctrl/bootreg reset path not understood -
  documented TODO; no IRQ claimed).

  select MFD_SYSCON), bindings for the reboot node and a new hisilicon,luofu-sysctrl syscon node.

  same value back, only when the low byte is the measured 0x10/0x11 A/B encoding (0x21 untouched,
  never invents the stock value); (2) write the vendor softrst_val0/1 pair 0x51162100/0xaee9deff
  to the CRG reboot word at page offset 0x00; (3) if that does not take, arm the CRG watchdog

  shared syscon regmaps; probe performs no register access; writes confined to selector/reboot/
  watchdog words (never soft-reset 0x84, mux, PLL).

  correctly; no consumer code change needed.

## 2026-11-18 16:55 - 0x21 selector semantics integrated, patch 017 corrected, boot-time pair recorder added, final image rebuilt (362ca4ec) and install harness 100/100

0x21 research (opensource/docs/SELECTOR-0x21.md, 926 lines incl. resolution section; 129 [V]/20 [U]/
6 [X]): reconstructed from read-only U-Boot disassembly, env dumps and bench records:
- The selector is the 32-bit SYSCTRL cell 0x10100C08; the env blocks (enva mtd3/envb mtd4, one
  128 KiB block each crc32-le(4)|flags(1)|data(131067)) hold bootcmd=bootflag pair selection.
- The env bootflag is the ACTUAL pair selector; the cell is the failure record. The loader prints
  bootflag/bootreg, initialises the cell from env when 0 (10/11), and bootfip stores the OPPOSITE
  pair's low byte before Linux starts (0x11 for an A boot, 0x10 for B). A recorded value that
  contradicts env means "last boot of that pair failed": loader re-stamps env to the other pair
  and boots it. A successful boot therefore requires userspace to re-record the running pair
  (vendor hsd_appm boot_done, ~16-30 s).
- 0x21 is the PROJECT'S bench value (FLASH-PLAN/fire-device), not vendor-written; the vendor
  userspace writes only 0x10/0x11. 0x21 boots B when env=b, bootfip then stores 0x10, and 0x21
  never persists; a true POR clears the cell to 0 (43/43 POR sequences). A 0x21/bad handover
  cannot strand the box (RESET-hold/TFTP recovery is entered after a POR that clears the cell).
- Driver/installer implications: patch 017's claim that the vendor writes 0x21 was unsupported;
  the store must be a low-byte RMW preserving the upper 24 bits (upper meaning [U]); and our
  target was missing the boot-time pair-recorder service, so the installer's two-witness check
  would refuse on our own system and the first reboot after a normal boot could silently flip
  pairs.

Selector fixes (patch 017, sha c991aaa50419f4b6ba0c9a37018a682c0a7a5afc66d43c611c947af25cce0f1d):
- corrected comments/ABI/Kconfig/YAML: 0x21 = project bench value, env selects and cell records
  failure, vendor writes only 0x10/0x11; store is now a low-byte RMW preserving upper 24 bits with
  whole-cell read-back; probe remains register-free.
- new target image service base-files/etc/init.d/luofu_record_pair (START=96, enabled as
  S96luofu_record_pair): determines the booted rootfs slot from UBI mtd_num + /proc/mtd label
  (optional ubi.mtd= cross-check), bounded wait for the selector sysfs, maps to pair a/b, writes
  the running pair, logs, idempotent, fail-safe (never manual-b/uninitialised/unknown, never
  touches env/mtd/devmem).
- platform.sh comments corrected (env is the selector; handover via the loader mismatch path;
  two-witness valid because of the recorder; non-fatal warning if the recorder is absent;
  refusals unchanged). Harness extended with recorder scenarios: 94/94 fixture assertions and
  100/100 with the real rebuilt container.

Upstream review-form series regenerated consistently: commit message 0017 rewritten, series/0017
and 01-commit-messages regenerated via gen-series.py --check, validation logs/hashes replaced,

Decision (owner, 2026-11-18): the 2026-10-01 GPL source request has had no reply and is no longer
tracked as an open project action or gate. Rationale recorded: GPL is a real copyright license but
enforcement is private civil action, not a project dependency; we redistribute no vendor binaries
and our drivers are our own code with provenance markers, so the only practical effect of no reply
is that source cannot accelerate the LSW/PIE/Wi-Fi work. The request page is kept as a
provenance/licensing record and as an optional lever (follow-up/escalation text remains ready if
ever wanted), but no waiting and no enforcement-org route is planned. The project continues
